description: MIXING and MASTERING: each part levelled, panned, high-passed, given its depth on a shared reverb, mastered to a loudness target — a WAV AND `mixgraph`, the mix as a document. After doseedo_render_score pass from_job (its parts and the instruments they play are the stems); or stems: [{name, audio_url, instrument?}]. An orchestra (strings / winds / brass / timpani / harp…) is SEATED by default (film-orchestral: violins left, low strings right, brass behind, each seat at its depth in a 2.3 s hall, written dynamics riding the faders); others mixed blind. style: film-orchestral, film-orchestral-sections, film-scoring-stage, concert-hall, film-epic-hybrid, cathedral-choral, classical-chamber, cartoon-studio, golden-age-cartoon, jazz-combo, jazz-strings, big-band, ambient, country-pop, metal-modern, 1950s-mono, 1960s-lcr-pop, 1970s-analog-rock, 1970s-dub, 1980s-pop-gated, 1990s-rock-dry, 1990s-hiphop, lofi-hiphop, 2000s-loudness-rock, 2010s-edm, 2010s-trap, 2020s-pop, 2020s-hyperpop, 2020s-tech-ad (id or words). guitar_tone = guitar sound. balance {part: dB} moves parts on top of the levelling (+3 = a melody forward). Change the mix: edit the returned mixgraph — strips[] {stem, gain_db, pan, seat, chain, sends}, buses[] (verb = the hall; a section's fader_db = its level), master.chain, automation [{target: "strips.<stem>.gain_db", points: [[seconds, dB]…]}] for rides (dB off the strip's gain_db: 0 = as set, -60 mutes) — and call again with mix_job (this job_id) + only your edits (or the whole mixgraph + the same stems): rendered as written, rails reported, no credits. Then doseedo_session_from_stems {from_job, mix_job: <this job_id>} → the DAW project at this mix's levels and pans. TO PICTURE: dialogue (the VO; the music ducks under it), music_offset_s (bar 1 on the picture), length_s (cut + end fade). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~15–90 s). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running mix — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

balance.description: {part name: dB in -12..12} — your balance on top of the levelling (and of the written dynamics a from_job reads).

bpm.description: The music's tempo: a guitar tone's echoes (an eighth, a dotted eighth) land on it. from_job fills it.

dialogue.description: The VO / dialogue on the picture's timeline (≤ 4): [{name?, audio_url}]. The music ducks under each line until the voice sits duck.vo_over_db over it, with a 1–4 kHz carve while it talks; the voice joins after the music's master chain. Report: output.dialogue.lines [{start_s, end_s, duck_db, vo_over_music_db}] as mixed.

duck.description: How the music sits under the dialogue: {vo_over_db (default 7 dB — a broadcast mix's 6–10), carve_db (default 3, at 1–4 kHz), max_db (default 12), include (default true; false = the music bed alone, ducked as if the voice played)}.

dynamics.description: Fader rides from written dynamics: {part name: [[onset_seconds, velocity 0-127], …]}. from_job fills it from the score (pp to ff ≈ 17 dB); pass {} for no rides.

dynamics_carried.description: {part name: top velocity} — parts whose stems already play their written level (a render part's dynamics_level receipt, up to its top_vel). Their rides count it: no doubled swing. from_job fills it.

dynamics_ride.description: How hard the written dynamics move the faders: 1 = default (pp to ff ≈ 17 dB), 0 = no rides, up to 1.5.

end_fade_s.description: With length_s: the fade at the program's end (0–10 s, default 0.5).

from_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_render_score job_id — its parts are the stems, each with the instrument it plays, and each part's written dynamics (its mean velocity) set its balance.

from_jobs.description: MCP: ONE cue rendered as several doseedo_render_score jobs (its parts split across renders): every job's parts are the stems, balanced and ridden by their written dynamics as one score.

guitar_tone.description: The guitars' and bass guitar's own SOUND. Every guitar and bass-guitar part (an upright played pizzicato too; never a synth bass or an 808) gets a tone by default ("auto"): a mixing chain for the style — compression, the amp's voicing and speaker, chorus / phaser / tremolo, its own echo and reverb, in stereo — fitted to that stem (drive only where the genre is driven, and less on a take that already came out amped; an acoustic gets EQ, compression and a room, never an amp; a bass stays centred and dry). "none" = as rendered (dry, mono). Or name one: a tone id, or words ("surf", "dark trap loop", "80s chorus") — for every guitar, or {part name: tone} for one. Tones — electric: clean-studio, pop-shimmer, funk-quack, funk-phaser, disco-chank, neo-soul, motown-soul, jazz-archtop, jazz-fusion, country-twang, country-ballad, surf-drip, desert-twang, rockabilly-slap, fifties-tweed, sixties-jangle, british-chime, psychedelic-swirl, soft-rock-phase, eighties-chorus, city-pop, new-wave-flange, post-punk-chorus, grunge-chorus, dream-pop, indie-jangle, math-rock-clean, emo-twinkle, reggae-skank, ska-upstroke, dub-skank, afrobeat-clean, soukous-sparkle, bachata-requinto, cumbia-psych, gospel-clean, rnb-smooth, edm-funk, hiphop-sample, lofi-tape, trap-ambient, ambient-swell, cinematic-clean, prog-clean, blues-edge, blues-lead, heartland-edge, indie-rock-edge, worship-dotted, post-rock, seventies-crunch, southern-rock, slide-delta, alt-rock-crunch, britpop-wall, grunge-rhythm, eighties-arena-lead, synthwave-lead, shoegaze-wash, pop-punk-rhythm, punk-raw, metal-rhythm, metal-lead, djent-tight, doom-fuzz, garage-fuzz · acoustic: acoustic-natural, acoustic-pop-strum, acoustic-fingerstyle, acoustic-intimate, acoustic-country, acoustic-bluegrass, acoustic-rock, acoustic-celtic, acoustic-12-string, acoustic-lofi, acoustic-cinematic, acoustic-hiphop-loop, acoustic-worship, acoustic-latin-strum, acoustic-blues, acoustic-gypsy-jazz · nylon: nylon-bossa, nylon-classical, nylon-flamenco, nylon-latin-pop, nylon-lofi, nylon-cinematic · steel: pedal-steel-country, pedal-steel-ambient, lap-steel-island · bass: bass-studio, bass-sixties-thump, bass-finger-funk, bass-slap, bass-picked-rock, bass-driven-rock, bass-metal, bass-dub, bass-jazz-electric, bass-fretless, bass-eighties-chorus, bass-hiphop, bass-lofi, bass-country, bass-indie, bass-dance, bass-latin, bass-cinematic · upright: upright-jazz, upright-slap, upright-folk, upright-sampled, upright-latin, upright-cinematic. The mix says what it chose and why: mixgraph.provenance.guitar_tones {part: {tone, why, read, drive}}; the chain is the strip's own (strips[].chain), editable like the rest.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

length_s.description: The program's length (a :30 = 30; ≤ 600 s): the mix is cut there with end_fade_s (default 0.5 s); the room's tail never runs past it.

mix_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_mix job_id to edit — its whole stored mix (every ride) is the base, mixgraph is applied on top, and its stems are reused when you pass no from_job / stems.

mixgraph.description: An edited mix — the mixgraph a doseedo_mix returned, changed — rendered against the same stems (from_job or stems). With mix_job: ONLY what you change (strips[] by stem, automation[] rides by target — points: [] removes one, buses[] by id, master) — the rest is that mix as stored. A mixgraph marked `partial` (its rides summarized) is refused without mix_job. Omit for a fresh mix.

music_offset_s.description: Where bar 1 of the music sits on the picture (seconds, ≤ 600; the program ≤ 600 s): every music stem — and its rides — starts this late; the dialogue does not move.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

print_sections.description: Also print every section as its own stem: output.section_stems [{name, members, url}] — a 24-bit WAV per section (its players, their room and hall share, through the mix's own master), and the dialogue as one; the prints add up to the mix (report.prints.sum_error_db). Sections are the mix's group buses (film-orchestral-sections: strings / woodwinds / brass / percussion / keys_harp; parts in none print as "other"). About twice the render time; no extra credits. Works with mix_job too.

room.description: An orchestra's room: "studio" (intimate scoring stage, ~1.2 s, close), "stage" (~1.8 s), "hall" (the default scoring hall, ~2.3 s), "cathedral" (~4 s, wet) — or 0..1 between them. Sets the decay, size and how wet every seat sits.

stems.description: [{name, audio_url, instrument?}] — the stems (≤ 32). instrument = the sound it plays (a doseedo_instruments id: "violin", "timpani", "harp"), which decides how it is mixed; without it the name decides.

style.description: A mix style: an id or words ("dry 90s rock"). Pick it for the picture — the default (film-orchestral, a 2.3 s scoring hall) suits film drama, not every orchestra: film-orchestral-sections = the same hall, the strings and winds seated wider, a fader per section (buses[].fader_db); cartoon-studio = a cartoon / animation orchestra (a close, dry, wide scoring stage, punchy rides); golden-age-cartoon = a 1940s–50s cartoon (mono, small studio, tape); film-scoring-stage = intimate TV / documentary; concert-hall; film-epic-hybrid = trailer / action; cathedral-choral; classical-chamber; 2020s-tech-ad = a tech / product / brand film (sleek modern electronic, matched to official tech ads); or jazz-combo (a small jazz band), big-band (a big band, seated in sections), ambient, 1970s-analog-rock, 2020s-pop …

target_lufs.description: Master loudness, -24..-6 LUFS (default: the style's — -18 for film-orchestral, -14 for the blind default). Met within ~0.3 LU (a loud target clips the shortest transients first); output.loudness says what landed, and why when short. With mix_job it re-masters the stored mix.

tonal_match.description: Nudge the master toward professionally mixed orchestral references (default on for the orchestral styles). Its presence and air are judged only where the score is written loud (written_level), so a pp passage keeps its darkness.

vintage.description: A period medium over any style, after the mix: "tape" = 7.5 ips tape (saturation, wow and flutter, a low hiss); "shellac" = a 78 played back (mono, ~90 Hz–5.5 kHz with the reproducer's presence, a 1.3 Hz wow, surface noise that swishes once a turn, crackle). "none" takes a style's own medium off (golden-age-cartoon carries tape). Its node (master.chain type vintage: noise_db, crackle, hi_hz …) is editable in the returned mixgraph.

written_level.description: [[seconds, velocity], …] — the whole score's written level, the loudest part sounding, held until the next row (0 = nothing plays). The tonal match reads only the passages it writes loud (f and louder), so a pp passage keeps its darkness. from_job fills it.

name: doseedo_mix
title: Mix and master stems
